title: Fossils and Past Environments
seo_title: Grade 3 Fossils Worksheets: What Fossils Tell Us About Life Long Ago
standard_text: Analyze and interpret data from fossils to provide evidence of the organisms and the environments in which they lived long ago.
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets on fossils (NGSS 3-LS4-1): kinds of fossils, extinct organisms, and how fossils show what past environments were like, with rock layer pictures. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Fossils show what lived long ago and where.
key_sub: Seashells in a desert mean the land was once under the sea. Fossils are evidence of past life and past environments.
body_html:
How to think about it

Fossils are the remains or traces of living things from long ago: bones, shells, leaf prints, footprints and insects in amber.

Fossils are evidence of what lived long ago and what the environment was like. Seashells in a desert mean the desert was once ocean. Palm leaves in Antarctica mean it was once warm. Many fossils are of extinct organisms, like dinosaurs and woolly mammoths.

Example

Fossil fish are found on a dry hill. What was the hill like long ago?

Fish live in water.

Answer: It was under water.

Example

Is a woolly mammoth extinct?

None are alive today.

Answer: Yes.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the fossil environment is the same as the environment today.
  • Thinking all fossils are dinosaurs.
  • Thinking a fossil is the living animal.

faq.a: A fossil is the remains or traces of a living thing from long ago, like a bone, shell, leaf print or footprint.

faq.q: How do fossils tell us about past environments?
faq.a: If ocean fossils are found on land, the land was once under water. If palm fossils are found in a cold place, it was once warm.
An extinct organism no longer lives anywhere on Earth, like dinosaurs and woolly mammoths.

items.q: What does extinct mean?
c: no longer living anywhere on Earth
items.e: Dinosaurs are extinct.

items.q: What can fossils tell us?

what kinds of living things lived long ago and what their environment was like
what the weather will be tomorrow
items.e: Fossils are evidence of the past.

items.q: Noah reads a fossil card: “An insect was trapped in sticky tree sap that hardened.” What kind of fossil is this?
items.e: An insect in amber.

items.q: Which body parts most often become fossils?

items.e: Hard parts last longer.

items.q: Emma studies a fossil of a woolly mammoth. It looks most like which animal living today?
items.e: A woolly mammoth and an elephant have similar body parts.

items.e: Extinct organisms are known only from fossils and records.
